Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Threat.value: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened

vignette: Raj, a 29-year-old South Asian shopowner, had been struggling with the aftermath of physical abuse by his romantic partner. The trauma from that experience had profoundly altered how he perceived and interacted with his environment, especially in his daily life running his store. One day while stocking shelves at his shop, Raj was hit with a wave of intense rage as a customer's body odor triggered an intrusive memory of the event. He found himself feeling threatened by the stranger approaching him, even though it was just a regular interaction about buying some items. The smell and the sudden recollection plunged him into a state of panic, making him question his ability to cope with such ordinary situations. Raj had come to believe that his body kept reacting as if he were still in danger, despite being safe. This belief intensified his sense of threat, especially at night when the darkness made it harder for him to feel secure. He often woke up drenched in sweat from nightmares and found himself unable to fall back asleep, tormented by images of what had happened. The triggering moments seemed random and unpredictable-certain conversation topics or even a specific smell could instantly bring back the full memory without warning. When these memories surfaced, Raj felt an overwhelming sense of rage but also an intense guilt over not having done more to stop the abuse. This inaction guilt gnawed at him, reinforcing his belief that he couldn't rely on himself. Raj's partner's physical abuse had left lasting scars both physically and emotionally. He remembered specific instances where certain odors or topics would instantly bring back the full memory of the event, causing intense rage and making it difficult to maintain composure in public. These memories often led to sleep problems, as he found it harder to feel safe at night. The more Raj felt threatened by strangers and in general, the more he experienced triggers that sent him spiraling into those intrusive memories again. He was certain that his body's reactions were beyond his control, further deepening his sense of helplessness and fear. This cycle of threat, memory, and self-doubt had become a constant presence in his life. At his shop, Raj's interactions with customers often became fraught as he found himself on edge, constantly vigilant and reactive to any small trigger. He dreaded the night shifts, when his vigilance spiked, making it even harder for him to function normally. The combination of threat from strangers, sleep problems, and intense memories had turned what was once a routine part of running his business into a daily ordeal. Despite these struggles, Raj's partner continued to push him to handle tasks at the shop alone, which only exacerbated his fears and self-doubt. He felt like he couldn't rely on himself, and this fear made it even harder for him to trust anyone around him. Each time he experienced an intrusive memory or was triggered by a conversation topic or smell, he would feel an intense wave of guilt over not having done more to stop the abuse. Raj finally decided to seek help when his relationship with his partner deteriorated further and his work performance began to suffer significantly. He was most afraid that he wouldn't be able to overcome these overwhelming feelings and continue running his shop successfully. Yet, he also hoped for relief from this constant cycle of fear and memories, so he could regain a sense of control over his life. The tight loop of triggers leading to threats, triggering more intense memories, and reinforcing negative appraisals had become the core of Raj's daily struggles. He was desperate for help to break this self-reinforcing cycle and find some semblance of peace.
